entry.title: Next.js API routes vs route handlers: when to use each
entry.summary: Next.js API routes vs route handlers is one of those migrations that looks trivial in the docs but bites you on caching semantics and runtime defaults. Both surface HTTP endpoints inside a Next.js project, but they sit in fundamentally different mental models — one is a Node.js request/response wrapper, the other is built on the Web Fetch API and plays by App Router rules. Pages Router API routes live at pages/api/**/*.ts. They receive a NextApiRequest (a thin wrapper over Node's IncomingMessage) and a NextApiResponse. The runtime is always Node.js. They are never statically analysed for caching by the framework — every request hits your serverless function. App Router route handlers live at app/**/route.ts. They receive a standard Request and return a standard Response. Because they are W…

entry.title: Why I Built a Zero-AI, Zero-Algorithm Q&A Space for Distraction-Free Thoughts
entry.summary:
Have you ever opened social media, scrolled for 30 minutes, and closed it feeling even more drained than before? Between AI-generated slop, rage-baiting algorithms, and endless ads, the internet often feels less like a space for connection and more like a loud, neon-lit casino. A few weeks ago, after feeling overwhelmed by digital noise, I decided to code a small, quiet, dark-themed Q&A corner for myself and fellow web users who miss the simpler web. It's called Ask A Monk: https://askamonk.online
🧘 What makes it different? Inspired by the quiet atmosphere of a monastery, I built Ask A Monk around three core principles: Zero AI & Zero Algorithms: Every question and response comes from a real human being. There are no recommendation engines pushing controversial content to keep you hooked. Complete Anonymity: No accounts, no sign-ups, and no social pressure for likes or upvotes. Distraction-Free UX: A minimalist dark UI with warm typography that is gentle on your eyes. 🛠️ The Tech & Philosophy I wanted to build something that feels fast, light, and completely free of modern bloatware. The interface focuses strictly on readable content and seamless navigation. Whether you're looking for perspective on a personal dilemma or simply want to draw a quiet daily thought, it's a space meant for slowing down. Feel free to stop by, draw a quote, or leave a question: Visit Ask A Monk] I'd genuinely love to hear your thoughts on the UI, UX, or the overall concept. How do you escape the noise on the modern web?

entry.summary: Gravity Mainnet, a fully EVM-equivalent Layer 1 with sub-second finality and 12,000+ TPS, is now available on Quicknode. Learn about its native oracle, agent-focused design, and how it evolved from Gravity Alpha Mainnet.
